title: SPICE: JPL's Observation Geometry System
description: SPICE is NASA JPL's Navigation and Ancillary Information Facility (NAIF) system for observation geometry: it organizes and computes where spacecraft, planets, and instruments are and where they point. Missions from Cassini to Mars rovers plan observations with it. The Toolkit (CSPICE, Icy, SpiceyPy) is free and the kernels are archived publicly.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: SPK Kernels: Positions and Velocities
description: SPK kernels store ephemerides — position and velocity of bodies and spacecraft as functions of time, usually as Chebyshev polynomial segments. One file can cover a whole mission. SPICE interpolates the polynomials to any requested epoch. This is the 'where is it' half of geometry.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: CK Kernels: Attitude History
description: CK kernels store attitude — orientation as a function of time, as quaternions or matrices with angular velocity. Spacecraft CK plus instrument-frame definitions tell you exactly where a camera pointed for every image. Without CK, pixels have no direction.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: PCK, FK, and IK: Frames and Instruments
title: PCK, FK, and IK: Frames and Instruments
description: PCK kernels carry planetary constants and body orientations (pole direction, prime meridian); FK kernels define reference frames and their relationships; IK kernels describe instruments (field of view, pixels). Together with SPK/CK they complete the geometry chain from planet to pixel.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: SCLK and LSK: Time Kernels
description: SCLK kernels convert spacecraft clock ticks to ephemeris time; LSK kernels carry the leapsecond table for UTC conversion. Time in SPICE is a first-class kernel problem because every position query needs an epoch. A stale leapsecond kernel shifts all your UTC tags.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: DSK: Digital Shape Kernels
description: DSK kernels store digital shape models — triangulated plates of asteroids, comet nuclei, and small moons — so SPICE can compute illumination, occultation, and surface intercepts on lumpy bodies. Ray-plate intersection against the shape model answers 'what pixel sees what rock.'
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: CSPICE: The C Toolkit
description: CSPICE is the C implementation of the Toolkit: spkezr for states, pxform for frame transforms, ilumin for lighting angles, occultation routines, and dozens more. It is the reference implementation everything else ports. Mission software links it directly.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Geometry Finder: Events Without Propagating
description: SPICE's Geometry Finder searches kernel data for events — occultations, eclipses, lighting conditions — over time windows without propagating anything: it roots-finds on geometry functions. 'When is the next Earth occultation as seen from the orbiter?' is one call. Mission planning runs on these searches.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Illumination Angles: Incidence, Emission, Phase
description: ilumin-style computations give incidence (sun-to-surface), emission (surface-to-observer), and phase (sun-surface-observer) angles for any surface point at any time. Camera exposure, science quality, and thermal input all key off these three angles. Every image is planned against them.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Occultations and Eclipses
description: SPICE occultation routines test whether the line of sight between two bodies clears a third — Earth occultations kill comms, solar eclipses kill power. Link budgets and battery sizing assume these blackouts. Geometry, not guesswork, sizes the margins.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: SPICE on Mars Missions
description: Mars rovers and orbiters plan every observation with SPICE: rover mast pointing uses surface frames and CK-like attitude, orbiter relay passes use occultation searches, and entry-descent-landing analyses use SPK trajectories. The same kernels serve science planning and operations.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Kernel Production and Archiving
description: Kernels are produced by missions and archived at NAIF: reconstructed SPKs from tracking data, CKs from attitude telemetry, and predicted kernels for planning. Versioning matters — reprocessing with better kernels changes science results. The archive is the permanent record of where everything was.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Validating Geometry: The Closed Loop
description: Geometry validation closes the loop: predict an occultation with SPICE, then observe the signal drop at the predicted second. Image a star field and check the camera pointing solution against CK. When predictions match observations repeatedly, the kernel set is trusted.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Writing Your Own SPICE Queries
description: A SPICE user loads kernels (furnsh), asks for a state (spkezr), transforms frames (pxform), and unloads — four steps that answer most geometry questions. Scripts chain these into planning tools. The Toolkit rewards the discipline of loading exactly the kernels a question needs.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The Full SPICE Geometry Chain
description: The ladder-top SPICE picture: kernels encode positions, attitudes, frames, shapes, and time; the Toolkit interpolates and transforms; the Geometry Finder searches events; missions plan observations, comms, and power on the answers. Fifteen rungs up, that chain flies every deep-space mission JPL operates.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.
